Why a corrected c-statistic is reported without an interval

Source: R/validation.R
mm_no_corrected_interval.Rd

DeLong's standard error is for an apparent c-statistic computed once on one sample. A corrected index is an apparent one minus an average optimism, and neither rms::validate() nor mm_full_process() returns the distribution of that difference, so there is nothing here to put an interval around.

Usage

mm_no_corrected_interval()

Value

One sentence.

Details

The recognised answer is a nested bootstrap: an outer loop resampling the cohort, each iteration running the whole correction, and a percentile interval taken over the corrected values it produces. That is B times the work of the correction itself and is not implemented. Reporting it as absent, with the reason, is what keeps the apparent row's interval from being read down the column as though it applied here.
